_supported_lanes_rationale: nvfp4_cb is DECLARED NOWHERE for this arch on purpose, and this note is the re-enable condition. The CB export lane is servable only where the pinned external Gridbook runtime names the architecture in its packaged runtime_contract.json producer_profiles.supported_ids; at the pinned 0.8.11 that set is [deepseek_v4, hy_v3, laguna, qwen3, qwen3_5, qwen3_5_dense], and glm5_next is absent from it in EVERY released Gridbook through 0.9.0 and on gridbook main -- the identifier does not occur anywhere in that tree. Declaring the lane anyway is the failure mode base.supported_export_lanes documents: the run COMPLETES and the artifact serves uninitialised memory, coherent garbage rather than a crash (commit 9a79963, Laguna). That is why test_gridbook_runtime_contract::test_declared_cb_lanes_are_a_subset_of_gridbook_supported refused this branch, and the refusal was correct: principle 9 makes serving reality the gate, and principle 14 makes the supported_ids table the attestation rather than our own belief about the runtime. RE-ENABLE by adding "nvfp4_cb" back here in the same commit that advances the Gridbook pin to a release whose supported_ids contains glm5_next -- not before, and not by widening the test. Nothing shipped depends on this: the 2026-08-27 GLM-5.3 campaign served through the compressed-tensors lane (4.683 bpp, TP=2 dense-MLA teacher, validator PASS).

_verified_source_layout.note: Provenance for this spec. Every claim below was read off the real checkpoint at /mnt/shared/models/GLM-5.3-Flash (model.safetensors.index.json, 76108 keys, plus safe_open metadata on shards 1/2/3) or off transformers 5.16.1 modeling code. Nothing here is inferred from a sibling architecture.

bf16_leaves: self_attn.kv_b_proj (12 MLA layers - NO scale sibling)
lm_head, embed_tokens, all norms, mlp.gate (router), hc_*, index_kpool_compress_*
fp8_source.per_tensor_not_per_leaf: o_proj is BF16 on the 34 KDA layers and FP8 on the 12 MLA layers. Any leaf-name-keyed source-dtype map is WRONG for this checkpoint; key on the presence of the .weight_scale_inv sibling in the index.

conversion_mapping.merge_execution: The two merges are executed on load by two generic, profile-driven bridges in prismaquant/layer_streaming.py, neither of which names this architecture: the per-expert merges by the packed-expert bridge (_pack_per_expert_into_packed, wired from moe.per_expert_regex + packed_experts.projection_splits), and the q/k/v_conv1d merge by the N->1 concat bridge (_merge_concat_sources, wired from the concat_merges block above). checkpoint_to_live_name is 1:1-or-drop and passes the source keys through unchanged so the bridge can see all three side by side.
conversion_mapping.not_renamed: MLA (q_a_proj, q_b_proj, kv_a_proj_with_mqa, kv_b_proj, o_proj) and indexer (wq_b, wk, weights_proj) already ship live spellings - unlike DSv4, which renames wq_a->q_a_proj.

serving_restriction.note: Why pinned_names is large. This is a principle-9 GATE INPUT, not a preference: the only vLLM serving path for glm5_next is PR #53906 (ZJY0516/vllm@933876c), and in that model file only routed experts, shared experts and dense MLPs are constructed with a quant_config. Every other Linear is built with quant_config=None, so a compressed-tensors re-export that quantized them would produce bytes the pinned runtime has no route for. Citations are to the PR tree, recorded so a gate can read them; re-attest against the pinned release before export (principle 14).

serving_restriction.CONTRADICTION_to_resolve_before_export: The PR's comment at model.py:329 says 'MLA projections are BF16 in checkpoint'. That is FALSE for the checkpoint at /mnt/shared/models/GLM-5.3-Flash: q_a_proj, q_b_proj, kv_a_proj_with_mqa and o_proj all carry .weight_scale_inv on all 12 MLA layers (48 scale keys) and are F8_E4M3 on disk; only kv_b_proj is BF16. Pinning them therefore means FP8_SOURCE passthrough at ~8.002 bpp, NOT BF16 - principle 11 forbids synthesizing BF16 from an FP8 source. Either the PR was written against a different checkpoint revision or it mis-loads these tensors. Resolve on the pinned runtime before pricing an artifact.

mass_split.measured_from: all 76108 index keys, safetensors headers of every shard, 2026-08-26; a .weight_scale_inv is counted in its weight's bucket
mass_split.passthrough_note: layer 45 (nextn/MTP, 288 routed + 1 shared expert = 7272923136 params) + the vision tower. Shipped VERBATIM at source precision via passthrough_prefixes; passthrough in v1 is a SCOPE choice, not a route fact - the PR DOES wire quant_config into Glm5NextMTP's experts (attested at 933876c, Codex-adjudicated 2026-08-26); quantized layer 45 is a legitimate post-v1 follow-up. A naive layers.[0-9]+.mlp regex counts these experts as quantizable and overstates the quantizable set by 7272923136 params.
mass_split.note: Neither the pinned nor the passthrough bucket can be dropped to BF16 where it is FP8 (principle 11), so 20.80 GiB is a floor, not a budget knob. Whole-artifact weight bytes ~= quantizable_params * bpp / 8 + 20.80 GiB: 181.1 GiB at 4.50 bpp, 190.0 GiB at 4.75 bpp.

open_todos.fused_groups: MLP gate/up fusion ATTESTED 2026-08-27 by direct read of the pinned runtime source (vllm-glm5next:pr53906-933876c, models/glm5next/nvidia/model.py:116 Glm5NextMLP.gate_up_proj = MergedColumnParallelLinear; the same class serves dense-layer MLPs and mlp.shared_experts). Both quantizable gate/up families are declared above so union-find promotes them to one format - a split assignment cannot load. KDA q/k/v fusion remains undeclared: the checkpoint's modules_to_not_convert hints (self_attn.qkv_proj 34x, fused_qkvbfg_a_proj 34x) match no index key, and every KDA projection is BF16-source pinned, so promotion over such a group is trivially satisfied.
open_todos.mtp: Layer 45 is the single num_nextn_predict_layers block. transformers 5.16 refuses it outright (modeling_glm5_next.py:1359 _keys_to_ignore_on_load_unexpected = [r'layers\.45\.', r'layers\.\d+\.shared_head\.']). It is body-indexed, not 'mtp.'-prefixed, so the mtp.* sidecar machinery does not apply - hy_v3 precedent: ship it VERBATIM via passthrough_prefixes with has_mtp() False.
